Repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui — 55 commits ahead of develop, 47 files, +4541/-105, plus 12 uncommitted files from a fix pass.

YOUR JOB: build a SCOPE LEDGER. Map the entire diff against the user story. You are not assessing code quality — three sibling agents cover cost, missing work, and the audit process. You answer one question: **what did we build, and does the story ask for it?**

=== THE USER STORY: SFCC-55 "Global Footer UI" ===

"As a Shopper, I want to see a consistent global footer on every page, so that I can access navigation links, contact information, legal content, and newsletter sign-up from anywhere on the site."

SCOPE STATEMENTS (verbatim — these bound the work):
- "It is CMS-managed via Contentful... **Contentful integration is covered in a separate user story.**"
- "**This story covers the footer shell, layout, and component structure only** — footer link destinations, email sign-up Omneo integration, and Cookie Settings behaviour are covered in separate stories."
- "Links like ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY are only relevant on the AU storefront, however, **for the purpose of this user story we can include whatever placeholder links we want** and can use the design as a first set of links."
- "There is a footer design for both desktop and mobile."
- Rollout: AU, ME, EU-Domestic, EU-International, HK, UK, US-Domestic, US-International
- ASSUMPTION: "**We will build the footer structure first, without any content behind the different links and buttons.**"
- NOTE: "Keep in mind that the minimum size of that email sign up button is taken into consideration for accessibility purposes"

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
AC1 footer displayed at the bottom of every page, desktop and mobile
AC2 desktop: nav links in columns (ABOUT, CONTACT, HELP) per Figma
AC3 hovering a nav link underlines that word/those words
AC4 mobile: nav columns stack vertically per Figma
AC5 Stay in Touch section shows an email input field and submit button **as a placeholder component**
AC6 bottom bar shows Zimmermann wordmark, region/currency indicator, copyright text, legal links per Figma
AC7 (Site Merchandiser) merchandiser can define the footer links per storefront when setting up the storefront in SFCC

=== YOUR METHOD ===

1. Get the full file list: `git diff origin/develop --name-only` plus `git status --porcelain`.
2. For EVERY file, and for the significant blocks within the large ones, assign exactly ONE category:
   **[R] REQUIRED** — an AC cannot be met without it. Name the AC.
   **[S] SUPPORTING** — not named by an AC but genuinely necessary to make a required thing work (e.g. a theme recipe the styling rules mandate, a token the layout needs). Name what it supports and why it was unavoidable.
   **[D] DEFERRED** — the story's own text explicitly assigns it to a different story. QUOTE the excluding sentence.
   **[U] UNMENTIONED** — the story neither asks for it nor defers it. It simply isn't in the story.
3. QUANTIFY. Give line counts per category (use `git diff origin/develop --numstat`). I want to know what percentage of +4541 lines each category represents. Approximate is fine for blocks inside a file; be exact at file level.
4. For the three biggest files, break down INTERNALLY — `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/theme/components/footer.ts`, and `overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx`. A file can be 70% required and 30% deferred; say so.

=== SPECIFIC THINGS TO CATEGORISE, because they are the contested ones ===
- The name-capture modal (`SubscribeModal`, `useSubscribeModal.ts`, `useSubscribeModal.test.tsx`, the 9 modal theme parts, the 2 modal stories, `PRIVACY_CONSENT_COPY`, `ACCESSIBILITY_DISCLAIMER_COPY`). Note it ships behind `enableNameCapture` defaulting false.
- The five ui-kit atoms + one molecule (`zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput`, `zimmInputAction`) and their stories. For EACH: is it consumed by the footer? How many times? Would the footer work without it?
- `theme/components/button.ts` — count the variants and sizes it declares, and count how many the footer actually uses.
- The `clearable` prop on `zimmTextInput` — count its consumers.
- The two `.woff2` font binaries + `theme/fontFace.tsx` + `fontFace.test.tsx` + the `_app-config` mount.
- The four chevron icons in `icons/zimm.tsx` — count how many the footer uses.
- `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` (+131/-58) and the `.claude/registry/*.md` churn.
- `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (+105/-11 uncommitted, plus whatever it was before).
- `overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts` + its test.
- `.storybook/main.js` and `.storybook/preview.tsx`.
- `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.cursor/rules/tier1FrozenFiles.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
- `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx` (14 lines, all comments).
- `contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts` — check its importer count.

=== ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS ===
- Quote the story text when you assign [D]. Do not assign [D] from memory.
- [S] is the category most open to abuse — for every [S], state what would BREAK without it. If nothing breaks, it is [U].
- Verify consumption claims by grep, not assumption. "Is this atom used by the footer?" is a countable question.
- Do not editorialise about quality. A well-built [U] is still [U]. A scrappy [R] is still [R].
- Where you are genuinely unsure between two categories, say so and give both readings.

OUTPUT: the full ledger as a table (file · category · AC or justification · lines), then the quantified summary by category as a percentage of the diff, then the internal breakdown of the three biggest files, then a short list of anything you could not categorise confidently.
